newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on harvest spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on harvest spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower on spillover pressure from other U.S. wheat markets, traders said.

Wheat values eased as winter wheat harvesting looked set to expand this weekend. But spring wheat avoided the broad losses seen in Kansas City and Chicago thanks to firm cash values and forecasts for dry weather in North Dakota.

"We didn't go down as fast as everybody else," an MGE trader said. "We also had pretty good commercial business on both sides. We had scale-down commercial buying and we had hedgers come in and unload hundreds and hundreds at a time."
MGE spring wheat settled 2-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with July down 3-3/4 cents at $3.79. New crop September lost 2-1/2 cents to close at $3.70.

Cargill Investor Services, Country Hedging and Linnco all bought at least one million Sept bushels. Linnco, Chicago Corp and Benson-Quinn all sold around one million Sept, traders said. Atwood/Peavey bear-spread one million bushels of Sept/July at 10 to 10-1/2 cents.
MGE spring wheat futures volume was estimated at 26.469 million bushels, up from Thursday's volume of 17.660 million.
